Understand the world: The laws of the universe are created by the chief god, who is good and so enormous that he desires his own self perpetually. Therefore, reasoning can lead to the deduction of your resurrection. You need only remember how human flesh was fashioned when both first parents were created.

The world we live in offers opportunities for mistakes, learning, growth, and creativity. When you die, you return to the good and are reincarnated with infinite chances to grow as souls. Jesus was resurrected, and so will we; life's purpose is to learn, make mistakes, and imagine new possibilities.

This reset through death allows rejuvenation and learning from errors. Think about all possible lifetimes and live accordingly. Make many mistakes to truly grow as a soul.

Leonardo da Vinci’s famous painting, The Last Supper, depicts Jesus before his betrayal and crucifixion by the Romans. Notably, there's a number 33133 in the painting, which aligns with a quotation from Lamentations: "For no one is cast off by the Lord forever; through he brings grief, he will show compassion. Great is his unfailing love; for he does not willingly bring affliction or grief to anyone."

Jesus came to remind us of our eventual forgiveness and encourage us to forgive others and love enemies. The gospel of Thomas, a unique voice, teaches poetic and divine messages that align with teachings from other prophets like Dante and Dashki.

From the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus preached the Beatitudes: "Blessed are the poor in spirit for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." He also stated, "You are the salt of earth. But if the salt loses its flavor, it can no longer be made salty again; it is fit only to be thrown out and trampled underfoot. You are the light of the world."
